make.name: Volkswagen
make.description: German carmaker founded in 1937, the core brand of the Volkswagen Group. Its electric cars started with the e-up! (2013) and e-Golf (2014); since 2020 they are the MEB-based ID. family, plus China-only ID. Unyx, ID. Aura and ID. Era sub-brands built by its Chinese joint ventures.

models.name: e-Golf
models.description: Battery-electric version of the seventh-generation Golf, sold from 2014 and built in Wolfsburg and Dresden (and by FAW-VW in China from 2019). A 2017 update raised the battery to 35.8 kWh; production ended in late 2020 and the ID.3 replaced it.

generations.name: Golf Mk7 e-Golf
generations.description: Launch e-Golf with a 24.2 kWh battery and 85 kW motor.

generations.name: Golf Mk7.5 e-Golf (facelift)
generations.description: 2017 facelift: 35.8 kWh battery, 100 kW motor, EPA range up from 83 to 125 miles.

models.name: e-up!
models.description: Battery-electric version of the up! city car, built in Bratislava and sold in Europe from 2013 (never in North America). A 2019 update more than doubled usable battery capacity; the up! family ended production in 2023.

generations.name: e-up!
generations.description: Original e-up! with an 18.7 kWh battery and 60 kW motor.

generations.name: e-up! (36.8 kWh)
generations.description: Second iteration announced September 2019: 36.8 kWh (32.3 usable) battery, WLTP range about 258-260 km, alongside the SEAT Mii electric and Škoda Citigo-e iV twins.

models.name: ID.3
models.description: Compact electric hatchback and the first MEB-platform car, built in Zwickau (and by SAIC-VW in China) since late 2019. Facelifted in 2023, then substantially reworked and renamed ID.3 Neo in April 2026; the GTX was replaced by an ID.3 GTI due in early 2027.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Original ID.3 launched in 2020 with 45, 58 and 77 kWh batteries and the launch-edition ID.3 1st.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: March 2023 facelift with a new front bumper and better interior materials; from 2024 new 52/59 kWh batteries and the GTX and GTX Performance.

generations.name: ID.3 Neo
generations.description: April 2026 overhaul renamed ID.3 Neo: ID. Polo-style light bar front, new interior with physical buttons, 50/58/79 kWh batteries and more power; GTX dropped for a GTI.

models.name: ID.4
models.description: Compact electric SUV on the MEB platform and VW's first global EV, on sale since late 2020 in Europe and 2021 in North America (built in Chattanooga, Tennessee from 2022 to April 2026). The 2024 model year brought the stronger APP550 motor and new software. VW ended US production in April 2026, and the ID. Tiguan replaces it in Europe.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Original ID.4 with the APP310 motor; 1st Edition launch model, 52/58/77 kWh batteries depending on market.

variants.name: Pro / Pro S / 1st Edition RWD (77 kWh, 150 kW; EU Pro Performance)
AWD Pro / AWD Pro S (US) / GTX (EU) (77 kWh, 220 kW)

generations.name: 2024 update
generations.description: Model-year 2024 update: APP550 rear motor (210 kW RWD, 250 kW AWD), 12.9-inch screen and new software; little exterior change.

variants.name: Pro / Pro S RWD (77 kWh, 210 kW; APP550)
AWD Pro / AWD Pro S (US) / GTX (EU) (77 kWh, 250 kW)

models.name: ID.5
models.description: Coupe-roofed version of the ID.4, revealed in November 2021 and built in Zwickau and Emden. Updated with the APP550 motor for 2024. Reports in 2025 said VW will drop it around 2027; Australia ended it after the 2026 model year.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch ID.5 with 77 kWh battery in Pro, Pro Performance and GTX form.

generations.name: 2024 update
generations.description: Model-year 2024 update with the APP550 motor (210 kW Pro, 250 kW GTX) and a new 52 kWh Pure.

models.name: ID.6
models.description: Three-row, seven-seat electric SUV on the MEB platform sold only in China since 2021, in two versions: the ID.6 Crozz from FAW-VW (built until 2026) and the ID.6 X from SAIC-VW.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Revealed April 2021 (Shanghai). Rear-drive with about 63 kWh or 83-85 kWh CATL NMC packs, or dual-motor AWD.

variants.name: ID.6 Crozz Long Range RWD (84.8 kWh)
ID.6 Crozz Long Range AWD (84.8 kWh)
ID.6 X Long Range RWD (83.4 kWh)
ID.6 X Long Range AWD (83.4 kWh)

models.name: ID.7
models.description: Large electric liftback (and, from 2024, the ID.7 Tourer estate) on the MEB platform, built in Emden since 2023 as the electric successor to the Passat saloon and Arteon. It was planned for North America but VW cancelled its US and Canadian launch in January 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: World premiere April 2023; Pro (77 kWh) and Pro S (86 kWh) with the 210 kW APP550 motor, GTX with AWD, and the Tourer estate from 2024.

models.name: ID. Buzz
models.description: Retro-styled electric minivan inspired by the Type 2 Microbus, built in Hanover since 2022. Europe got a short-wheelbase five/six-seater first; the long-wheelbase seven-seater launched in 2024 and was the only US version (2025 model year). VW skipped the 2026 model year in the US and says the van returns later.

sources.name: Jalopnik (Dec 2025): no 2026 model year for the US

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Production from June 2022; 2024 update brought the 79/86 kWh batteries, 210 kW APP550 motor, LWB body and GTX.

variants.name: Pro LWB / US Pro S (86 kWh, 210 kW)

models.name: ID. Buzz Cargo
models.description: Panel-van version of the ID. Buzz with a bulkhead behind the front seats and room for two Euro pallets, sold in Europe since 2022.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Short-wheelbase cargo van, first delivered November 2022.

models.name: ID. Polo
models.description: Front-wheel-drive electric supermini on the MEB+ (MEB Entry) platform, built in Pamplona, Spain, and the first VW EV to take an existing nameplate. It is the production version of the 2023 ID.2all concept, unveiled in April 2026 from about EUR 25,000, with a 226 PS GTI.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Pre-sales from 29 April 2026; 37 kWh LFP or 52 kWh NMC battery, front motor.

models.name: ID. Cross
models.description: Subcompact electric SUV, the battery-electric counterpart of the T-Cross, sharing the ID. Polo's MEB+ hardware. Shown in September 2025, built in Pamplona from September 2026 and on sale in Germany from July 2026 orders.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launched with the 155 kW / 52 kWh version; 37 kWh LFP versions follow.

models.name: ID. Tiguan
models.description: Electric compact SUV that replaces the ID.4 and ID.5, built in Emden on the MEB+ platform. Fully unveiled in October 2026; Europe first, the US 'at a later date'.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Successor to the ID.4 with new Pure Positive design, triple-screen interior and 58/77 kWh batteries.

models.name: ID. Every1
models.description: Entry-level electric city car previewed by the ID. Every1 show car in March 2025, targeting about EUR 20,000 and due in 2027 as the e-up!'s spiritual successor. The production name is not confirmed (reported as ID.1).

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Planned for 2027 on a front-drive MEB Entry derivative; not planned for the US.

models.name: ID. Unyx 06
models.description: China-market version of the Cupra Tavascan coupe SUV, built by Volkswagen Anhui and sold under the ID. Unyx sub-brand (gold VW badge). Launched July 2024 as the ID. Unyx and renamed ID. Unyx 06 in April 2025; the 2025 model added a 53.6 kWh battery.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launched July 2024 from CNY 209,900; 2025 model adds a cheaper 53.6 kWh version.

models.name: ID. Unyx 07
models.description: Mid-size electric sedan from Volkswagen Anhui, related to the ID.7 but with China Electrical Architecture electronics; in production since January 2026 and updated for the 2027 model year in October 2026 with a larger 77.5 kWh battery.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Rear-drive, 170 kW, LFP batteries; 2027 update adds lidar ADAS and a 77.5 kWh pack.

models.name: ID. Unyx 08
models.description: Full-size five-seat electric SUV co-developed with XPeng on XPeng's platform, previewed as the ID. Evo concept in 2025 and on sale in China since April 2026; refreshed with lower prices in September 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Production from March 2026; 82 or 95 kWh CATL LFP batteries, RWD or AWD, up to 315 kW DC charging.

models.name: ID. Unyx 09
models.description: Full-size electric executive sedan from Volkswagen Anhui with XPeng-supplied driver assistance, unveiled at Auto China in April 2026 and launched on 24 October 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 92 kWh CATL LFP battery with 800-volt electronics; RWD or AWD.

models.name: ID. Aura T6
models.description: Mid-size electric SUV from FAW-Volkswagen's ID. Aura sub-brand, effectively the China successor to the ID.4; unveiled April 2026 and launched 20 September 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Rear-drive 170 kW on MEB with China Electrical Architecture; 59.9 or 77.5 kWh LFP.

models.name: ID. Aura L5
models.description: Mid-size electric liftback sedan for FAW-Volkswagen's ID. Aura sub-brand on the China-specific Compact Main Platform, previewed by the ID. Aura concept (2025) and revealed through MIIT filings in October 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Single- or dual-motor, 155 kW motors, 175 km/h.

models.name: ID. Era 5X
models.description: Compact battery-electric SUV from SAIC Volkswagen's ID. Era sub-brand on the China-only Compact Main Platform; production started 20 October 2026 with market launch due in November 2026. (The other ID. Era models are plug-in hybrids or range extenders and are not listed.)

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Rear-drive, 155 kW UAES motor, CATL LFP 45.8 or 58.5 kWh.

models.name: e-Lavida
models.description: Battery-electric version of the SAIC-Volkswagen Lavida compact sedan for China, introduced in 2019 with a 38.1 kWh battery.

generations.name: e-Lavida
generations.description: Electric Lavida based on the third-generation (2018) Lavida.

models.name: e-Bora
models.description: Battery-electric version of the FAW-Volkswagen Bora compact sedan for China, based on the fourth-generation (2018-2026) Bora, with about 270 km of rated range.

generations.name: e-Bora
generations.description: Electric version of the fourth-generation Bora.

models.name: e-Caravelle
models.description: Battery-electric passenger version of the seventh-generation Transporter, developed with Ford (Tourneo Custom twin) and built by Ford Otosan in Turkey since 2024.

generations.name: T7
generations.description: Rear-motor EV with a 64 kWh battery; L1/L2 lengths, 100-210 kW, AWD added later.

models.name: e-Transporter
models.description: Battery-electric panel van version of the seventh-generation Transporter (Ford Transit Custom twin), built by Ford Otosan in Turkey since 2024.

generations.name: T7
generations.description: Rear-motor EV with a 64 kWh battery; 100, 160 or 210 kW.

legacy_notes.note: Legacy 'ID.4 1st Edition' (2021) mixed eras: EPA 291 mi and 125 kW DC match the 2024+ APP550 car, while price $41,420 and 201 hp-class specs belong to 2021-2023; the 2021 1st Edition was EPA-rated 250 mi (fueleconomy.gov). Claimed on the 2021-2023 77 kWh RWD variant. Power column (335) is the 2024+ AWD figure, not this car.

Legacy 'ID.Buzz 1st Edition' is the US long-wheelbase 86 kWh RWD van (EPA 234 mi, 2025 MY). Legacy carmodel_first_released 2021-03-01 is wrong (production from June 2022, US sales June 2024). VW built no 2026 model year for the US.

Legacy 'ID.7 1st Edition' with EPA 300 mi and $50,000 is not a real US car: VW cancelled the ID.7 for North America in January 2025, so it never got an EPA rating or US price. Its full_slug duplicates the ID.4 row ('vw-id-4-1st-edition') and vehicle_class 'SUV' is wrong (it is a liftback sedan). Claimed on the European ID.7 Pro (77 kWh, 210 kW).

gaps: ev-database (HTTP 429) and the shared web-search budget ran out mid-research, so several 2026 variants lack prices, WLTP ranges or 0-100 times (ID.3 Neo 58 kWh, ID.7 59 kWh, ID.4/ID.5 2026 model year, e-Caravelle/e-Transporter).

US MSRPs for ID.4 model years 2021-2025 and the 2025 ID. Buzz 4MOTION were not sourced; only the 2026 ID.4 Pro ($45,095, vw.com) and 2025 ID. Buzz Pro S ($59,995, vw.com) are filled. Connector type for 2025-2026 US models (NACS vs CCS1) not verified.
ID.4 2024-2025 US Standard (62 kWh): EPA lists a 210 kW motor while Wikipedia says 62 kWh cars kept the 150 kW APP310; power left null.
ID. Buzz US status: VW skipped the 2026 model year; vw.com still shows the 2025 van (Nov 2026). Return timing (2027 vs 2028) is disputed, so the US market is left 'current'. Please re-check.
ID.4 China (ID.4 Crozz / ID.4 X) and ID.3 China (SAIC-VW) specs and current status not researched; Wikipedia names the ID. Aura T6 as the China successor of the ID.4.
e-Lavida status (still on sale or not) could not be verified and is marked current; e-Bora battery and range cycle not sourced. ID. Unyx 06 per-variant specs and prices not sourced.
ID. Every1/ID.1 production name and specs are unconfirmed; only the 70 kW motor and ~EUR 20,000 target are reported.
Not included: e-Crafter (2017-) and ABT e-Transporter T6.1 (commercial vans, status unverified); ID. Era 9X/8X (range extenders) and ID. Era 5S (plug-in hybrid) are excluded as not battery-electric.
No verified free photo for: ID.5 2024 update, ID. Every1, ID. Aura L5, ID. Era 5X (Wikimedia rate limits also limited the search).
